messages:
Samir Rao: Kicking off Cobalt evaluation thread. They want 1k sustained qps with p95 < 200ms for short prompt completions. Need a quick plan for queueing behavior tests + cost tradeoffs.
Jess Yoon: Got it. Do we know average tokens per request?
Paula (sales): Cobalt said ~30 input tokens, ~70 output tokens. Most calls are independent (no long multi-turn).
Matt O'Neill: Recommend testing with rw-medium-v2-q4 and rw-medium-v2-fp16 as a compare. Quantized will lower cost but may add ~10-20ms.
Liza Chen: For queueing, we'll simulate burst patterns + steady 1k qps. Important: KV cache hit-rate will matter if they reuse prefixes. Ask them about duplication.
Samir Rao: They do some dedup in-app but expect ~10% cache hits. Plan both 0% and 10% scenarios.
Jess Yoon: I'll draft load plan. Quick sketch: 1) ramp to 1k qps over 3m, 2) hold 10m steady, 3) apply 5x burst for 2m, 4) drain. Also run steady 250/500 qps baselines.
Matt O'Neill: Load tool: vegeta is fine. Something like:
```
echo 'POST /generate' | vegeta attack -rate=1000 -duration=10m -targets=targets.txt | vegeta report
```
Include payloads with varied lengths.
Liza Chen: Runtime config to test:
``
--batch-size=8
--max-latency-ms=200
--kv-cache=true|false
--concurrency=auto
```
Samir Rao: Also measure queue length (requests waiting in the router) and queueing latency per-token. Those are the customer’s primary concern.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for rw-medium-v2-q4 on dedicated-pool-3 (canary id: can-2026-03-10-09).
Jess Yoon: Quick cost calc for hosted path vs dedicated reserved: assume token cost hosted $0.0008 per output token, dedicated marginal infra cost ~ $0.0002/token when saturated. For 1k qps * 70 tokens * 3600s = ~252M tokens/hour => hosted ~$201.6k/hr (obv unrealistic for long run; need reserved).
Matt O'Neill: Those numbers look off — recheck: 1k qps * 70 tokens = 70k tokens/sec -> 252M tokens/hr correct. But hosted pricing scales with model. We'll present hourly burn and monthly committed options.
Paula (sales): Cobalt expects monthly estimate and a recommended committed tier. Provide both 6/12 month reserved options + outage fallback.
Liza Chen: From perf side, early run results (1k qps ramp + hold) on dedicated-pool-3 rw-medium-v2-q4:
- achieved throughput: 980 qps sustained
- p50: 42ms, p95: 178ms, p99: 430ms
- queueing latency (avg): 12ms
- KV cache hit rate simulated at 10% -> effective p95 down to 150ms
- errors: 0.12% (timeouts during 5x bursts)
Samir Rao: Nice. What about fp16 variant?
Matt O'Neill: fp16 run (same config):
- throughput: 1005 qps
- p50: 34ms, p95: 150ms, p99: 360ms
- errors: 0.05%
Tradeoff: fp16 gives ~15% latency improvement, slightly higher memory so fewer instances fit per GPU. Cost delta ~ +8% infra.
Jess Yoon: Add in a quantized + batching run (batch-size=16): saw p95 ~210ms under steady load, but cost/unit dropped ~30%. So for strict p95 < 200ms they might prefer fp16 dedicated; for cost-first they'd pick quantized with larger fleet.
Paula (sales): For SOW: include recommended config, fallback to hosted rw-medium-v2-fp16 when reserved capacity hits 90% and auto-scale timeout >2m. Also include a 3-tier pricing example.
Samir Rao: Enterprise blocker: Cobalt's security team flagged E2E encryption + data residency. They want VPC + KMS integration for keys and a SSO audit for the Private deployment. Any blockers on that?
Liza Chen: Private deployment supports KMS/HSM and SAML SSO. Onboarding timeline ~4-6 weeks. Need SOC2 artifacts + egress rules doc. I can attach the checklist.
Paula (sales): They also filled the security questionnaire — I'll drop it here later.
Matt O'Neill: Action items: 1) Jess run final 2-hour steady 1k qps run with fp16 and q4 with KV 0/10% (ETA EOD today). 2) Liza produce TCO slides (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with per-token and infra amortization. 3) Samir + Paula sync on SOW and compliance ask.
Jess Yoon: Starting the long run now. Will post results + vegeta output summary.
deploy-bot: Load test job started (job id: load-176543-01).
Jess Yoon: Early 30m snapshot: fp16 steady 1k qps -> p95 148ms, p99 375ms, errors 0.03%. Attaching short CSV in thread (will link in final writeup).
Samir Rao: Great. Once you have full run, share the 99/95/50 numbers and the queue length histogram. We'll convert to slides for Cobalt.
Paula (sales): I'm prepping a pricing appendix for 6/12/24 mo commitments with a burst SLA and support tiers.
Liza Chen: Also note: application-level retries amplify queueing — recommend client-side exponential backoff + jitter in SOW to avoid retry storms.
Samir Rao: Ok team, this is looking good. Jess — ping when final artifacts are in. I’ll schedule a short sync with Cobalt for Friday to present. :thumbsup:
Jess Yoon: Will do.
Paula (sales): Adding Cobalt contact (cc): @andrew.c (will DM).
Matt O'Neill: Quick FYI: we saw a pathological case at 5x bursts where a single slow GPU caused head-of-line issues; we mitigated with per-model request timeouts and per-instance circuit breakers. Note to include in ops runbook.
Samir Rao: Perfect — include that in the risk section. Closing thread once slides + CSVs uploaded. Thanks all. :rocket:
